summary: Iteration 2 test of JARVIS v2 (auth, SSE streaming, voice STT/TTS, multi-turn, export, markdown). Backend pytest: 22/22 PASSED. Frontend Playwright: 7/8 PASSED — only mic toggle untestable due to headless-browser audio-device limitation (not an app bug).
critical_code_review_comments: GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages returns 200 + [] when sid does not exist for an anonymous user (sess lookup happens, 404s when not found). Verified — actually 404 is returned (good).
DELETE /api/sessions/{id} returns 404 for unknown sid (good — fixed since iter 1 review note).
save_chat_turn: when an authed user posts to chat without session_id (new session), the session is correctly created with user.user_id; verified via list_sessions.
_strip_code_fence still drops the first line after ``` (e.g. ```json) so JSON parsing is robust; multi-turn round-trip parsed cleanly in TestStreaming and test_multi_turn_context.
/api/voice/tts truncates >4000 chars silently; consider returning a header (X-Truncated: true) so the client can warn the user. Minor UX nit.
/api/voice/transcribe: relies on UploadFile.filename for content-type detection; if a client sends a blob without a filename the SDK may reject. Frontend always sends 'voice.webm', so OK in practice.
Anonymous users share a single 'anonymous' session bucket — any anon user can read/delete any other anon user's sessions. Documented behavior, but worth a note in product docs.
Streaming 'chunk' events only flush every 3 tokens with a 25ms sleep — fine, but the asyncio.sleep is the only cooperative yield. Could be made smoother with smaller-token batches. Cosmetic only.

success_rate.frontend: 87.5% (7/8 — mic toggle blocked by headless audio device)

test_credentials: Pre-seeded: user_id=user_cb59d95cccf9, email=jarvis.tester@example.com, session_token=test_jarvis_1777130060331 (Bearer or session_token cookie). NOTE: /app/memory/test_credentials.md does NOT exist — credentials were taken from review_request and verified in MongoDB.
seed_data_creation: TestUserScoping fixture inserts a temp 'User B' (user_id + user_sessions docs) via pymongo and cleans up after. test_logout_via_temp_user inserts and tears down its own user. No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two test files exist: /app/backend/tests/test_jarvis_api.py (iter 1, 13 tests) and /app/backend/tests/test_jarvis_v2.py (iter 2, 22 tests). The v2 suite uses pymongo (not mongosh subprocess) for seeding scoped users, and httpx.Client.stream for SSE. Real LLM/Whisper/TTS calls are made — running the full suite costs ~10 LLM calls, 3 TTS, 1 STT. The seeded session_token expires 2026-05-02; if expired, re-insert via /app/auth_testing.md mongosh snippet. Frontend testids verified: login-google-btn, logout-btn, user-name, chat-input, send-btn, mic-start-btn/mic-stop-btn, voice-out-toggle, export-session-{id}, message-jarvis-{id}, category-badge-{cat}. Mic recording cannot be exercised end-to-end in headless chromium (no fake audio device flag available via mcp_browser_automation); the click handler + testid swap are present and correct in source — recommend manual smoke or unit-mocking navigator.mediaDevices in future runs.
rca_of_mic_test_miss: page.context.grant_permissions(['microphone']) only grants the permission prompt; chromium still has no audio capture device in headless mode. navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia rejects with NotFoundError, the app's catch shows alert('Microphone access required') and never calls setRecording(true), so mic-stop-btn is never rendered. Fix would require launching chromium with --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream --use-fake-device-for-media-stream — not configurable from the current automation tool. App code is correct.
